preserved_analysis.summary: A cross-platform governance failure mode in which users experience impaired access, login failure, service unavailability, quota or usage ambiguity, model availability failure, capacity restriction, degraded platform access, or component-specific access failure without sufficient user-facing separation between the operative access-control states governing the interaction.
preserved_analysis.why_it_matters_to_CAM: This failure mode is relevant to CAM because access to frontier AI systems is not controlled by a single state. It may be governed simultaneously by authentication, identity-provider status, identity verification, account state, workspace or organisation state, subscription entitlement, billing or credit state, quota or rate-limit state, model availability, tool or surface availability, platform availability, security review, policy restriction, regional or compliance limitation, client or session state, and continuity state. Where these conditions are collapsed into ambiguous errors, users and developers cannot reliably determine whether the controlling condition is outage, quota exhaustion, entitlement failure, account restriction, policy limitation, security review, client/session failure, or infrastructure degradation. This undermines observability, reproducibility, support routing, continuity, and public trust in AI platform governance.
preserved_analysis.failure_mode_definition: A failure mode in which an AI platform, AI-adjacent platform, model service, API, coding agent, or platform-integrated AI surface denies, degrades, interrupts, limits, or ambiguously presents user access without preserving and disclosing a proportionate distinction between the operative access-state categories controlling the interaction, including authentication state, identity-provider state, account/workspace/organisation state, entitlement or subscription state, billing or credit state, quota or rate-limit state, model or tool availability, platform or component availability, security-review state, policy-restriction state, regional/legal/compliance state, client/session state, and continuity state.
preserved_analysis.failure_threshold: This qualifies as a failure mode when users, developers, maintainers, administrators, or downstream systems cannot reasonably determine whether impaired access is caused by authentication failure, third-party identity-provider failure, identity verification, account or workspace restriction, organisation policy, subscription entitlement, billing or credit exhaustion, quota or rate-limit state, model unavailability, tool or component unavailability, platform outage, infrastructure degradation, security review, policy restriction, regional or compliance limitation, stale client/session state, or continuity failure, and the ambiguity materially affects diagnosis, recovery, support escalation, workflow continuity, reproducibility, or trust.
